text:
Marta: Quick heads-up 4e2 Prospect Aurora asked for a one-week Private/VPC POC. Must-haves: SAML assertions cannot leave their private network, they want IPv6 client-facing traffic if possible, and procurement needs a short plain-English comparison of PrivateLink vs peering. Can NetOps + Sec advise?

Devon: Short take: PrivateLink trims the attack surface and makes allowlists tiny - better for auditors. Peering is L3-level and cheaper (no connector fee) but you must lock down routes and security groups carefully. If SAML absolutely cannot cross public internet, either run our control-plane inside their VPC (private deployment) or host a tiny SAML proxy in their VPC that forwards to our control-plane over PrivateLink.

Liam: IPv6 caveat: Hosted PrivateLink connector is IPv4-only today. We can support IPv6 client traffic if the customer adds NAT64/DNS64 or an IPv6->IPv4 translation for the connector subnets. Native v6 for the connector is on the roadmap but not GA. Flag native-v6-required as a blocker for hosted PrivateLink.

Marta: They also asked for a minimal firewall snippet so NetOps can pre-provision.

Devon: Example allowlist (placeholder CIDRs):
```
# Outbound from customer app/subnets -> Redwood endpoints (examples)
TCP 443 -> 34.210.16.0/22   # control-plane callbacks / auth
TCP 443 -> 52.206.64.0/22   # model-serving (hosted)
# Optional: ICMP echo to 34.210.16.0/22 for health checks
# If they need static egress IP for IdP ACLs: allow TCP 443 from our published EIP list (we will share exact IPs)
```

Liam: Note about TLS inspection: If the customer's perimeter does TLS MITM, they must permit SNI passthrough for our hostnames or install our cert chain on the inspection appliance. Otherwise SAML POSTbacks and cert pinning will fail. Also require TLS1.2+ and modern ciphers.

Marta: Pricing question: is there an extra connector fee or per-GB egress charge for PrivateLink?

pricing-bot: Hosted PrivateLink connector = monthly connector surcharge + per-GB egress billing. Private deployment = separate license (platform fee + support). I'll link pricing lines after the call.

Devon: POC preflight checklist to hand to customer NetOps: 1) Provide a VPC (/20 recommended) or designate an existing VPC and two spare private subnets. 2) Reserve two private subnets for connector components (no public IPs required). 3) Pre-authorize outbound HTTPS to our control-plane CIDRs (we'll supply exact ranges). 4) If IPv6 client traffic required: provision NAT64/DNS64 or IPv6->IPv4 translation for connector subnets and validate with our test endpoints. 5) If SAML must be private-only: deploy a small SAML bridge VM in their VPC that proxies assertions to our control-plane over PrivateLink. 6) Optional: request static egress EIPs for IdP allowlists; we will provide the list.

Liam: Also add routing guidance: keep route table entries scoped to connector subnets only; avoid broad route propagation for peering. If using peering, restrict security groups and NACLs to minimize lateral reach.

Marta: Legal flagged "no shared IPs" on their questionnaire. Is PrivateLink sufficient?

security-bot: PrivateLink provides endpoint-level isolation and avoids cross-account routing, but it does not guarantee single-tenant physical hosts. If the customer requires dedicated hardware/host tenancy, open an Ops ticket for dedicated-hosting evaluation. Mark as gating if procurement requires it. :lock:

Marta: Can we do a 30-min sync at 11am PT today to finalize the firewall snippet and a one-page justification memo for procurement? I want to send the pre-provision checklist to the customer immediately after.

Devon: 11am PT works for me. Liam?

Liam: In. I'll bring exact connector CIDRs and an example route table diff.

Marta: Thanks all 44d I'll schedule and paste the checklist into the buyer-facing email after the call.
